min_stable_gain.conditions: Datasheet title 'Unity gain stable'; 1.4 GHz small-signal bandwidth at G = +1, RL = 150 ohm (pdf p.4).
what_datasheet_says_below_or_at_min: Unity gain in the SOIC (D) package 'may result in the device becoming unstable'; SOIC is suitable for gains >= +2 V/V or -1 V/V; TI recommends the leadless MSOP (DRB) or MSOP PowerPAD (DGN) for maximum performance (pdf p.31, Design Tools).

Fig 92 (pdf p.31): unity-gain follower, VIN = 100 mVpp, +-5 V, 150-ohm load: SOIC with Rf = 0 ohm peaks by about +17.5 dB near 650 MHz; SOIC Rf = 100 ohm about +10 dB near 500 MHz; SOIC Rf = 200 ohm about +8.5 dB near 380 MHz; leadless MSOP and MSOP with Rf = 0 ohm about +2.5 dB near 600 MHz (CURVE, +-1 dB).

The general gain-configurable EVM 'can be configured in a gain of +1; however, it is strongly not recommended ... may cause the part to become unstable'; stability can be controlled with a large feedback resistor at the cost of performance (pdf p.31). Fig 93: on that EVM peaking of about +16 dB (Rf = 0) to about +5.5 dB (Rf = 150 ohm) (CURVE, +-1 dB).
Peaking is attributed to lead inductance in the feedback path; recommended maximum feedback-path inductance 4 nH, with a trace-inductance formula (Eq. 8) (pdf p.32).
'nominally compensated to operate with a 2-pF parasitic load'; parasitic capacitive loads > 2 pF can begin to degrade performance; loads < 4 pF may not need an isolation resistor (pdf p.27-28).
No guidance is given on capacitive (TIA) feedback or noise-gain shaping; the datasheet contains no transimpedance example.

Fig 34 (+-5 V): 1-MHz triangle input (right axis +-2.5 V, output axis +-5 V, implying G = 2) drives the output into clipping at about +3.85 V and -3.85 V. In the linear part the output trace already lags the scaled input trace by about 0.35-0.4 V (about 20 ns at about 20 V/us). On release from the negative clip the output leaves the limit about 30 ns after the scaled input crosses the clip level, i.e. an extra lag of roughly 10-30 ns; the positive-side release shows no lag beyond the 20 ns offset.

Fig 70 (5 V single supply): clipping at about +1.43 V and -1.37 V on the plotted axis (presumably referred to mid-supply, giving about 3.9 V and 1.1 V absolute); negative-side release about 40 ns after the scaled input crosses the limit (about 20 ns beyond the standing offset).

packages.name: SOIC-8 (D, D0008A)
packages.notes: Unity gain in SOIC may be unstable (pdf p.31). Fig 91 caption uses theta_JA = 170 C/W for SOIC (different board assumption). Max ambient to keep die < 60C (Table 1): 28.8-33.7C.

packages.name: MSOP-8 PowerPAD (DGN, HVSSOP, DGN0008D)
packages.ep_connection: Must be connected to a thermally dissipative plane (pdf p.2 note 2); the PCB procedure says to connect all five 13-mil thermal vias to the internal ground plane with full (non-spoke) connections (pdf p.29). The electrical potential of the pad is not stated.
packages.notes: Recommended package (with DRB) for maximum performance; max ambient for die < 60C: 41.3-44.2C (Table 1).

packages.name: MSOP-8 (DGK, VSSOP, DGK0008A)
packages.notes: Table 1 gives max ambient of -10.2 to -23.2C to keep the die below the 60C oscillation limit, i.e. not usable at room temperature in that sense. Listed only for THS4271 in the 2025 addendum (THS4275DGK appears in the p.2 ordering table but not in the addendum).

packages.name: VSON-8 leadless MSOP (DRB, DRB0008A)
packages.ep_connection: 'The package thermal pad must be soldered to the printed circuit board for thermal and mechanical performance' (pdf p.53 note 3); potential not stated.
packages.notes: Max ambient for die < 60C: 45.3-47.6C (Table 1). MSL Level-2.

pinout_notes: THS4271: 1 NC, 2 IN-, 3 IN+, 4 VS-, 5 NC, 6 VOUT, 7 VS+, 8 NC (all packages D, DRB, DGN, DGK). THS4275: 1 REF, 2 IN-, 3 IN+, 4 VS-, 5 NC, 6 VOUT, 7 VS+, 8 PD-bar (pdf p.3). Standard single op-amp pinout, so the feedback resistor can sit between pins 2 and 6.
tia_content_note: No transimpedance example, figure, table or design equation in this datasheet. Relevant general material: noise model Fig 87 with Eq. 4 (total output noise) and Eq. 5 (input-referred), giving 12.2 nV/rtHz output and 6.2 nV/rtHz input-referred for the Fig 75 G = +2 circuit (pdf p.27); feedback resistors 249 ohm to 1 kohm recommended for most situations (pdf p.20); resistors above 2 kohm with about 0.2 pF parasitic can add a pole/zero below 400 MHz (pdf p.28).
application_guidance: Keep the die below 60C to avoid low-level oscillation (see other_notes); THS4211/THS4215 are the recommended replacements (pdf p.1, p.19).
Minimise parasitic capacitance on all signal I/O pins; open ground and power planes around the I/O pins (pdf p.28).
Decouple with 0.1 uF placed < 0.25 inch from the supply pins plus 2.2-6.8 uF bulk; 6.8-22 uF bulk, 0.1 uF and 1000 pF recommended per supply (pdf p.23, p.28).
Place the feedback resistor directly under the package on the opposite side between output and inverting input when double-sided mounting is possible (pdf p.28).

Capacitive loads: isolation resistor R(ISO) recommended; Fig 24 (pdf p.12): 25 ohm for 10 pF, 15 ohm for 50 pF, 10 ohm for 100 pF (RL = 499, +-5 V). Fig 88 (pdf p.27) pairs 15 ohm with 100 pF and 10 ohm with 50 pF (inconsistent with Fig 24; rev F says Figure 24 notation was corrected).
Load of 150 ohm to 1 kohm gives best distortion; terminating an ADC input in 50 ohm can be detrimental (pdf p.26).
abs_max_and_input_protection: VS 16.5 V; VI +-VS; IO 100 mA; TJ 150C max, 125C for continuous long-term reliability, 60C max to prevent oscillation; Tstg -65 to 150C; ESD HBM 3000 V, CDM 1500 V, MM 1000 V (pdf p.2). No statement on input-protection diodes or maximum differential input voltage. No thermal shutdown (pdf p.30).
other_notes: MAJOR CAVEAT: 'The THS4271 and THS4275 may have low-level oscillation when the die temperature ... exceeds +60C'; caused by the internal bias circuit, not mitigated by external configuration, occurs randomly with process variation and cannot be screened (pdf p.1, p.19). Table 1 (pdf p.19) gives the maximum ambient temperature for TJ < 60C at IQ = 27 mA and RL = 499 ohm: SOIC 28.8-33.7C, VSON 45.3-47.6C, PowerPAD MSOP 41.3-44.2C, MSOP (DGK) -23.2 to -10.2C. At +-5 V the quiescent dissipation alone is about 0.22-0.27 W.

THS4275 power-down: PD defaults to positive supply (amplifier on) when not driven; thresholds relative to REF: enable >= REF + 1.8 V, disable <= REF + 1 V when REF <= midrail; enable >= REF - 1 V, disable <= REF - 1.7 V when REF > midrail (Tables 2 and 3, pdf p.22-23). PD quiescent current 875 uA TYP (REF = 0, PD = REF + 1 V, +-5 V; MAX 1000/1100/1200 uA) or 650 uA TYP (PD = REF - 1.7 V, REF = VS+); 5 V: 650 uA TYP both. Turn-on 4 us, turn-off 3 us (50% of supply current). Power-down output impedance 200 kohm (+-5 V) / 100 kohm (5 V); PD input impedance 4 Gohm / 6 Gohm at 1 MHz (pdf p.5, p.7). Power-down is not a high-impedance output mode (pdf p.22).
SPICE model available; does not model distortion or package differences (pdf p.35).
